text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS

- Former prime minister and current Socialist opposition leader Felipe Gonzalez offers Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar pact to assure national cohesion in face of rising demands from minority regional parties.
- Regional government of Navarra defies central government and lowers tax on companies.
- Spain's ambassador to Israel is special European Union (EU) envoy to Middle East.
- War between squatters and police in Barcelona's Gothic quarter.
EL MUNDO

- Secret Civil Guard report says General Enrique Rodriguez Galindo, detained as suspect in killing of Basque separatists during 1980s "dirty war" against ETA, enriched himself through smuggling operations.
- Gonzalez and Aznar blame each other for instability of regional financing pact.
- Spain is first European country where anti-AIDS vaccine will be tried.
DIARIO 16
- Gonzalez offers pact to end "war" between regions.
ABC
- Government takes final step towards liberalising telecommunications.
CINCO DIAS
- King Juan Carlos to receive extra benefits in addition to 990 million peseta budget in 1997.
- Banco Santander announces sharp cuts in mortgage rates to lure customers from competitors.
EXPANSION
- Time Warner and Hughes negotiate participating in digital TV with Telefonica.
- Santander Group earned 71.8 billion pesetas attributable profit in first nine months, up 13.2 percent.
- Cajamadrid nine-month profit rose to 41.3 billion pesetas.
- EU to investigate Endesa buy offers for Sevillana and Fecsa.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Navarra joins fiscal chaos and lowers company tax to 32.5 percent from 35 percent.
- Aznar says reforms will be based on social dialogue with no pressure.
